title: Repertoire shift to Bunk Johnson and George Lewis tunes
summary: The Melbourne band's tunes came from Bunk Johnson and George Lewis records, replacing his earlier Oliver and Watters repertoire, played with a looser touch.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Did your repertoire change when you went into this Melbourne New Orleans jazz band much?

Oh yes, yes, yes. Most of the tunes were new to me actually. They were based on, mainly on the records, Bunk Johnson, George Lewis and those men made, whereas previously I'd been playing King Oliver, Lou Watter's sort of tunes.
What were some of the typical ones you were playing before the Melbourne band?
Well, Lou Watter's tunes like, I think of a tune, Friendless Blues. Oh gosh.
Well anyway, what have you been playing lately with the Melbourne jazz band?

Just for contrast, I'm trying to get in on it. Yes, with the Melbourne jazz band, sometimes my burden is so hard to bear, Lord, Lord, Lord, you've been so good to me. The ones that have been played and recorded over and over again by George Lewis and others. With we hope a slightly fresh touch and trying not to be a slavish copy at all. What can I say on a George Lewis kit, just trying to play in a looser sort of style than the old Lou Watter's King Oliver type, but not to just copy records, which doesn't make sense to my mind.
